commits.message:
[TritonGPU] Do not rematerialize volatile loads (#12268)

`canBeRematerialized` returns early for small loads before it checks for
write effects, so `RemoveLayoutConversions` can rematerialize a volatile
load. When the loaded value is used in several layouts, each layout then
gets its own read, and the uses can see different values.

Check write effects first, so the check added in #11001 also covers
loads. A volatile load that is only used in one layout now keeps its
layout and gets a `convert_layout` instead of being moved.

The new `no_remat_volatile_load` lit test fails without the change (two
`tt.load`) and passes with it. The full lit suite passes. With the
kernel from the issue on an L4, `num_warps=4` now emits one
`ld.volatile` instead of six, and 0 of 20000 readers are inconsistent
(19725 before).

Fixes #12256.

commits.message:
[NVIDIA] Account for BF16 mixed-precision adds in the vectorizer (#12304)

BF16-to-FP32 accumulation chains are currently costed as ordinary FP32
additions because `isFusedHalfAddition` only recognizes FP16 extensions.
On SM100, this can select packed FP32 additions that retain separate
BF16 conversions instead of folding them into mixed-precision adds.

Recognize BF16 extensions when computing the scalar addition-chain cost.
The predicate remains restricted to FP32 `FAdd`; FMA operand-type
matching is unchanged.

Add regression coverage for BF16 accumulation, both FP16/BF16 FMA factor
orders, and same-type FMA controls. The mixed-factor cases retain their
conversions and use ordinary FP32 FMA.

Validation:
- Full compiler lit suite: 305 passed, 2 unsupported plugin tests.
- 48 GB200 numerical/codegen cases passed, covering both factor orders,
contraction enabled/disabled, scalar and packed layouts, and FMA
followed by BF16 accumulation. None of the 24 mixed-factor cases emitted
`FHFMA`.
- Pre-commit checks passed.

commits.message:
[JIT] Hash source locations in cache keys (#11832)

## Summary

Make the JIT cache key follow one contract: a change to the kernel's
source or
source location, or to the line-info setting, gives a new compilation
cache
key.

| Source/location changed | Line-info setting changed | New compilation
cache key |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Yes | No | Yes |
| No | Yes | Yes |
| No | No | No |

This simplified contract and its implementation are from @Jokeren, who
pushed
them to this branch; they replace my earlier version, which hashed the
location
only when line info was emitted.

- `JITCallable.cache_key` always hashes the kernel's source file,
starting
line, and definition line and column, so a kernel that moves, or the
same
  source loaded from another file, gets a new key.
- The line-info setting is not hashed separately:
`TRITON_DISABLE_LINE_INFO`
is already a cache-invalidating environment variable, so changing it
alone
  also gives a new compilation cache key.
- Compile-warmup serialization keeps these fields when it rebuilds a
kernel.

Refs #11817. This fixes the stale source-location part. Under this
contract,
moving a kernel gives a new key even when line info is disabled, and
unset and
`0` still give separate keys, as on `main`.

## Testing

- `test_source_locations_invalidate_cache` (unchanged, file, line,
decorator,
and column variants, each with and without a line-info change) passed
10/10
  when compiled for a gfx1100 target. With `main`'s `jit.py`, the file,
  decorator, and column cases fail (6/10).
- A compile-cache check of the four rows above: the second compile
created a
  new cache entry exactly in the three "Yes" rows.
- `test_cache.py` and `test_driver.py` show no new failures relative to
`main`
  on a machine without a GPU driver.
- Pre-commit passed on all changed files.

These runs compiled on CPU for a gfx1100 target; no GPU execution is
claimed.

commits.message:
Split result tensor and bias arguments in test_core::test_dot kernel (#12271)

This PR splits input bias tensor and output Z tensor to avoid potential
data race.

Assume all warps process store dot results in similar layout as they
process it, so there are no LDS involved and no barriers in code.

This means one warp can do all the work and finish before other warps
read Z memory.
This can lead in data races in some ADD_COLS and ADD_ROWS cases, where
same pieces of input Z are used by different warps.

commits.comment: 修复 tensor descriptor 指针回退中大 shape 符号扩展导致负值的问题（#12255）。RewriteMakeTensorDesc 中 shape 原使用 castToI64（符号扩展），使 [2^31, 2^32) 范围的维度变为负数从而屏蔽掉所有非负访问。新增 castUnsignedToI64 辅助（arith::ExtUIOp），仅对 shape 使用零扩展，strides/padding 与 descriptor indices/offsets 继续用有符号扩展。新增 lit 测试 dynamic_shape 校验 arith.extui 生成并被 bounds check 使用。

commits.message:
[BACKEND] Fix large tensor descriptor shapes in pointer fallback (#12278)

## Description

Fixes #12255.

In-kernel tensor descriptors use signless i32 shape operands. When
descriptors are lowered to pointers, those operands were sign-extended
to i64, so dimensions in `[2^31, 2^32)` became negative and caused every
nonnegative access to be masked out.

Zero-extend descriptor shapes during `RewriteMakeTensorDesc` so their
nonnegative values are preserved. Descriptor indices and offsets
continue to use signed extension.

A minimal lit regression checks that a dynamic descriptor shape is
widened with `arith.extui` and used by the generated bounds check.

## Testing

- `pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD`
- `make PYTHON=.venv/bin/python MAX_JOBS=8`
- `lit -v test/Triton/rewrite-tensor-descriptor-to-pointer.mlir`
- `lit -sv test` (304 passed, 2 unsupported)
- Exact issue repro on NVIDIA A10 (sm_86) with the source build:
  - `M=2^31-64`: in-kernel `[1]`, host `[1]`
  - `M=2^31+64`: in-kernel `[1]`, host `[1]`
